messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: aes(size=levels(factor))
parts:
Adam, 

I'm not sure if this got answered or not yet, but you can suppress the legend from each geom_* by adding legend=FALSE outside of the aes(). Although, as pointed out the other day sometimes if you want to get rid of it completely, you might have

https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/wiki/Legend-Attributes
If you go there you should be able to set the appearance of each legend attribute. If these are not working, make sure that you do not have a general theme setting after you do your opts() call. I have made this mistake many times. 

ggplot+
geom_*()+
opts(legend settings)+
theme_bw()            #resets all the opts to the theme_bw() standards

B

messages.author: d588a03e58ea7e7f
messages.subject: Re: aes(size=levels(factor))
parts:
I don't think it possible just with ggplot. The closest you can get
is setting the legend.key option in the theme, but this just controls
the decoration around the displayed point. In particular, setting it
to theme_blank() does not suppress the key itself, just any decoration
around it.

If you know enough about grid graphics, it should be possible to go
back after the plot is made and change the underlying grid structure
to eliminate those grobs. I don't know grid well enough to say how to
do this, though.

--
Brian S. Diggs, PhD
Senior Research Associate, Department of Surgery
Oregon Health & Science University
